note: Market-intelligence Wardley input -- the FIFTH, FORWARD feed (spec stories 28, 32). Each component sits on a Wardley map: `visibility` is the value-chain Y axis (1 = user-facing, 0 = deep infra), `evolution` is the X axis (0 genesis .. 0.25 custom .. 0.5 product .. 0.75 commodity .. 1). `velocity` is per-year rightward drift (commoditisation speed). For an `attacker-capability`, moving right = the attack COMMODITISING = its cost COLLAPSING = the linked war-game risk's loss-event-frequency rising BEFORE the reactive feed reports a single landed incident. `base_risk` is the current (reactive) FAIR posture + deployed move; the layer projects the forward LEF from the commoditisation movement and hands the war-gamer a forward scenario to re-price. Editorial, grounded in named public trajectories (NIST PQC timeline, RaaS/PhaaS marketplace reporting), not a live subscription.

components.note: KNOWN-INERT (finding F2). Flags commoditising and emits nothing: _forward_risk() fires only for actor == attacker-capability, so a commoditising DEFENCE has no path to lower a cost, an LEF, or TCoR. Carried to make that gap visible on the map rather than buried in the source. Even if F2 were fixed, the commoditised half (transport key agreement) is not what pq-harvest-now-decrypt-later's costs.fix actually buys -- discovery/inventory, WebPKI signatures and boot roots of trust are the binding, stationary cost drivers.
